title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 221
paragraphs: Of this, the following strikes me as proof as convincing as any: Leonidas is known to have tried to dismiss even the soothsayer who accompanied the army, Megistias the Acarnanian — said to be descended from Melampus — so that he would not perish with them, after he had declared from the victims what was about to come upon them. Megistias, however, when ordered to leave, would not himself depart; but he sent away his son, who was with him in the army, besides whom he had no other child.
